advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether the step-identity model token should fall back to the workflow-level `model:` when the step declares none, so a workflow-default class is still attributed.
evidence: runs.py:154-156 `model=resolve_model(cfg, step=ctx.step.get("model"), workflow=ctx.workflow.get("model"))` — the resolver also consults a workflow-level class the ContextVar never sees
ABSENCE: no fallback to `ctx.workflow.get('model')` when the step declares no model, so a workflow-default class is unattributed
advisory.finding: The step-identity binding captures only the STEP-level `model:` token (`step.get('model')` / `model_ladder[0]`), but `resolve_model` also resolves a WORKFLOW-level `model:` when a step declares none (runs.py:154-156 passes `workflow=ctx.workflow.get('model')`). A step that inherits its model CLASS from the workflow default will therefore run on that class yet record no `model_class`, silently reintroducing the exact 'declared X vs fell through to cfg.model' ambiguity this feature exists to remove.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that `_effective_config` (or a runner run) with `req.config.model` empty-string and None falls back to `base.model` rather than substituting an empty model.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/runner.py:208-211: `requested = getattr(req.config, "model", None)` / `if not requested or requested == base.model:` / `return base` / `return replace(base, model=requested)`

Docstring documents a distinct behavioral contract for this branch: "An ABSENT or EMPTY requested model falls back to ``base`` rather than raising ... substituting an empty model would build a provider session for nothing and fail deep inside the SDK ... this branch exists for a direct library caller."

tests/unit/test_llm_model_per_request.py covers only differing-model (override), same-model (control), and no-mutation cases via `_cfg(model=...)` with non-empty models; `search_files` for `model=""` and `model=None` under tests/ returns no matches — the empty/None `requested` path is never exercised.
advisory.finding: The `_effective_config` empty/absent-requested-model fallback branch (`if not requested ... return base`) is untested; no test passes an empty-string or None `req.config.model`, so a regression that dropped the guard and substituted an empty model into the config copy would not be caught.
scenarios: A direct library caller constructs a RunRequest whose config.model is empty/None; the fallback-to-floor behavior is relied upon but unverified.
A future refactor inverts or removes the `not requested` guard, letting an empty model reach `replace(base, model="")` and fail deep in the SDK — no test turns red.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add two cases in tests/unit/test_llm_model_per_request.py asserting the resolved model equals `_FLOOR_MODEL` when `req_cfg` carries `model=""` and when a stubbed config has no `model` attribute, exercising the `not requested` branch of `_effective_config`.
